target.founder: Naveen Rao, Michael Carbin, Sara Achour, MeeLan Lee

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $475M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Chips & Semiconductors (found 0 same-stage, 1 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 12 same-sector peers exist in Chips & Semiconductors, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

methods.skip_reason: target revenue not on file (private companies rarely disclose)
methods.rationale: Public Semiconductors P/S median is 21.4x across 3 tickers. Cannot apply without target's revenue.

data.narrative:
Unconventional AI is a Seed-stage semiconductor company that has raised $475M to date, with founders including Naveen Rao and Michael Carbin. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 3 public semiconductor peers (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private companies in the chips sector, though narrow-filter peer matching proved insufficient for a robust median-comp approach.

Of three triangulation methods tested, only stage-progression proved applicable. Using total capital raised ($475M) as a proxy for current value and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $1.2B. Peer-median analysis was not executable; while 12 same-sector peers exist, filtering for stage alignment and comparable scale yielded fewer than three datapoints. Public-comp anchoring using the Semiconductors sector P/S median of 21.4x across the three public comparables could not be applied due to the absence of target revenue data—standard for private companies.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $1.0B to $1.4B, centered on $1.2B, based on stage-progression alone. This narrow methodological foundation reflects the data constraints inherent to Seed-stage private company valuation in a capital-intensive, pre-revenue sector. Key uncertainties include the absence of revenue or unit economics, insufficient private-company peer comparables at identical stage, and the reliance on raised capital rather than market-tested metrics. Further refinement would require disclosure of financial or operational milestones.
